# viewbus — full product reference

> The fastest way to debug Azure Service Bus. A fast, native desktop app for Windows and macOS. Free, local, private.
> This file concatenates the full content of viewbus.app for AI agents that
> want a single fetch. For the shorter product summary see /llms.txt.

---

## What viewbus is

viewbus is a native desktop app (Windows + macOS) for developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs working with Azure Service Bus day-to-day. It lets users:

- Browse Azure subscriptions and their Service Bus namespaces in a live, locally-indexed tree (multi-tenant aware).
- Peek and filter active and dead-lettered queue and topic messages without dequeuing them.
- Search message *bodies* across every queue, topic, and dead-letter queue in a namespace at once.
- Edit a message body/properties in a side-by-side diff editor, then resend it (single or filtered-bulk).
- Run bulk queue operations — purge, move-to-dead-letter, bulk resend, bulk delete — with a preview, live progress, an ETA, cancel, and a run history.
- Set background alerts that watch dead-letter counts per resource and notify before a backlog becomes an incident (opt-in).
- Drive everything by keyboard, including a system-wide spotlight search.
- Expose the index and live message queries to AI assistants via a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- Expose the same index to your own tooling via a local HTTP API on `127.0.0.1`.

All data stays on the user's machine — no telemetry, no cloud sync, no accounts.

### Key facts

- **Name:** viewbus, lowercase (the Windows installer and macOS bundle are named `ViewBus` for install-time stability; user-facing copy is lowercase)
- **Platform:** Windows 10 / 11 (x64) and macOS (Apple Silicon; Intel via Rosetta)
- **Price:** Free
- **Source:** Closed source; distributed via the Microsoft Store, Homebrew, and GitHub Releases
- **Privacy:** No telemetry, no backend servers, no accounts
- **Built with:** Tauri 2, Rust, React, TypeScript, SQLite
- **Author:** Håkon Lia, an independent developer in Norway. viewbus is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Microsoft.
- **Current version:** See https://viewbus.app/latest.json

### Who it's for

Developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs who work with Azure Service Bus day-to-day and want something faster and more capable than Paolo Salvatori's Service Bus Explorer (still maintained, but Windows-only, .NET Framework, and with no message-body search) or the Azure Portal's built-in Service Bus Explorer (limited search, no cross-resource view, low peek caps).

### Differentiators vs alternatives

- **vs Service Bus Explorer:** native on macOS as well as Windows; message-body search across queues/topics/subscriptions at once; edit-and-resend with a side-by-side diff; background dead-letter alerts; an MCP server and a local HTTP API for automation; VS Code theme import; manual connection strings in the OS keychain.
- **vs the Azure Portal:** finds a message across every resource at once, no 100-message peek caps, background alerting, reaches namespaces outside the user's tenant via connection strings, keyboard-driven bulk operations.
- **vs Microsoft's official Azure MCP Server:** that server exposes Service Bus metadata (counts, status) but cannot peek dead-letter messages or trace a message across queues; viewbus's MCP server can, because it reuses the local index and the credentials the desktop app already holds.
- **vs custom SDK scripts:** a polished GUI with a persistent local index and spotlight search — no code required for common operations — plus a documented local HTTP API when you do want to script it.

---

## Feature detail

### Fast tree browsing

Subscriptions, namespaces, queues, and topics are indexed locally in SQLite. Navigation is instant, even on enterprise tenants with thousands of resources, with no round-trip to Azure for typical browsing after the initial index. If the account spans several Azure tenants, viewbus enumerates them and lets the user switch from the account dialog; the tree, search, and MCP results all stay scoped to the active tenant. The sidebar is tabbed — Subscription, All, Favorites, and Connections (manual connection-string namespaces).

### Browse and act on messages

Peek active and dead-letter messages without dequeuing. Filter by session ID, message ID, correlation ID, subject, or dead-letter reason. Edit a message's body and properties in a side-by-side (Monaco) diff editor before resending, or compose brand-new messages with full property and content-type control, including scheduled sends.

### Bulk queue operations

Purge an active queue, move every active message to the dead-letter queue, bulk-resend dead-lettered messages back to their entity, or bulk-delete by filter. Every operation previews the matching batch first, then runs with live progress, a running ETA, and a cancel button; throttling from Service Bus is handled with backoff rather than failing the run. The Operations tab keeps a history of everything that has run against a resource.

### Cross-resource message search

Search message bodies (not just resource names) across every queue, topic, and dead-letter queue in a namespace at once — the fast way to trace a stuck order by its ID without opening each queue by hand. Neither Service Bus Explorer nor the Azure Portal can do this.

### Background monitoring and alerts

Opt-in. Pick exactly which queues, topics, and subscriptions to watch and which should alert. viewbus samples dead-letter counts in the background (low cost to the machine) and fires a native notification when a resource crosses its threshold — so a backlog surfaces before it becomes an incident. Noisy alerts can be muted for an hour or a day; mutes auto-resume.

### Spotlight search and keyboard shortcuts

`Ctrl+I` (rebindable) opens a system-wide fuzzy search across every indexed resource — queues, topics, subscriptions. It stays active even when viewbus is minimized to the system tray, so it behaves as a global OS-level launcher for the Service Bus topology. Shortcuts throughout the app are customizable from settings.

### Built-in MCP server

viewbus ships a Model Context Protocol server over stdio transport. Any MCP-aware AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code Copilot, opencode, custom agents) can list namespaces, search resources, count messages, and peek bodies — over local stdio, no cloud round-trip. Settings → MCP generates a ready-to-paste config snippet per client. Full setup guide: https://viewbus.app/mcp-server

### Local HTTP API

While the app is running it serves a small HTTP API on `127.0.0.1` for external tooling. Full reference: https://viewbus.app/developers

- **Discovery:** on launch the app writes the port and a freshly generated bearer token to `local-api.json` in its config dir (`%APPDATA%\viewbus\` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/viewbus/` on macOS, `~/.local/share/viewbus/` on Linux).
- **Auth:** send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server binds `127.0.0.1`, requires the token, and rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header — so it is reachable from your machine only, never from the network or a web page.
- `GET /v1/status` → `{ app, apiVersion, version, hasSelection }`.
- `GET /v1/search?q=…&limit=…` → indexed queues, topics, and subscriptions with paths and last-known active / dead-letter counts. `limit` defaults to 20, max 50.
- `POST /v1/focus` with `{ id }` → brings viewbus to the front on that resource. Unknown ids return 404.
- Errors share one shape: `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, with codes `bad_request` (400), `unauthorized` (401), `forbidden` (403), `not_found` (404), `internal` (500).
- `/v1` is stable and additive-only: fields are only added, never removed or renamed. Breaking changes would ship under `/v2`. Enabled by default; disable with `localApi.enabled: false` in `settings.json`.

### Themes and VS Code import

Dark, light, or custom user themes. A one-click importer pulls the active VS Code theme into viewbus. Custom themes drop into the `themes/` subfolder of the settings directory as JSON files.

---

## MCP server tools

The MCP server is built into the desktop app (Rust, stdio transport). Ten tools are read-only and always enabled; one write tool is opt-in via a settings toggle.

Prerequisites: run the desktop app at least once (the MCP server reads the index it builds) and select a subscription. Every tool except `get_status` is scoped to the selected subscription and errors if none is chosen.

### Index and search tools (work even with the app closed)

- `get_status` — index state: whether a subscription is selected, last refresh time, resource count, and `liveQueryAvailable`. Call this first to orient.
- `list_namespaces` — indexed Azure Service Bus namespaces in the selected subscription.
- `list_queues` — queues under a given namespace.
- `list_topics` — topics under a given namespace.
- `list_subscriptions` — subscriptions under a given topic.
- `get_resource` — full details for a single indexed resource by ID.
- `search_resources` — fuzzy-search queues, topics, and topic subscriptions by name or path.

### Live message tools (require the desktop app to be running)

These proxy through the running app over a local socket, so Azure credentials stay in one place.

- `count_messages` — how many messages match a filter, optionally broken down by dead-letter reason. Returns numbers only, never bodies. Use this rather than peeking whenever the question is "how many".
- `peek_messages` — message summaries without dequeuing: sequence number, enqueued time, subject, message / correlation / session IDs, delivery count, dead-letter metadata, body size, property keys, and a short body preview. Hard-capped at 100 summaries per call; paginate via `fromSequence`.
- `get_message_detail` — the full body plus all custom and system properties for one sequence number.

Filters shared by count and peek, all applied inside viewbus so message bytes never enter the model's context: `bodyContains` (case-insensitive substring), `timeFrom` / `timeTo` (enqueued-time range, ISO 8601), `sessionId`, `messageId`, `correlationId`, `subject`, `deadLetterReason`, and custom `properties`.

### Write tools (opt-in)

Write tools are gated behind the `general.mcpThemeWritesEnabled` setting and default to off.

- `upsert_theme` — let an AI author themes by writing JSON files to the user's themes directory.

Message-level writes from MCP (resend / delete / send) are deliberately not implemented.

### MCP security model

- **Read-only against your bus.** No send, delete, resend, dead-letter, or purge tool exists. A peek is a non-destructive browse and does not change delivery counts.
- **No new credentials.** The MCP binary never talks to Azure directly. Live queries go through the running desktop app over a local-only socket, using the sign-in already present in the app. Browse and search read straight from the local SQLite file.
- **Local only.** stdio to the MCP client, a local socket to the desktop app. No network listener.
- **Subscription-scoped.** Tools only see the subscription selected in the app; references to resources in other subscriptions are refused.

---

## Install

### Windows — Microsoft Store (recommended)

https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0q5zmlv15k — the package is re-signed by Microsoft, so there's no SmartScreen warning, and it auto-updates through the Store.

### Windows — direct installer

The NSIS `.exe` on GitHub Releases. It isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first launch — click "More info" → "Run anyway" once; subsequent launches are silent. Resolve the current URL from the update feed or the releases page rather than hardcoding a version.

### macOS — Homebrew (recommended)

```
brew install --cask haakofli/viewbus/viewbus
```

A `.dmg` is also published on GitHub Releases. It isn't notarized by Apple yet, so on first launch macOS reports it as damaged / unverified. Clear the quarantine flag once with `xattr -cr /Applications/ViewBus.app`, or right-click the app → Open → confirm. Homebrew installs clear this automatically.

### Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, x64; or macOS on Apple Silicon (Intel via Rosetta 2).
- An Azure account with read access to your Service Bus namespaces, or a connection string per namespace.
- Outbound HTTPS to `login.microsoftonline.com`, `management.azure.com`, and your `*.servicebus.windows.net` endpoints.

### Programmatic resolution (recommended for agents)

```
curl https://viewbus.app/latest.json
```

Returns JSON with `version`, per-platform download URLs under `platforms` (`windows-x86_64`, `darwin-aarch64`), a top-level `installerUrl` (direct Windows `.exe`), `installerFormat` (`nsis`), `signed` (boolean), and `publishedAt` (ISO-8601). AI agents and update-checkers should read this file to resolve the latest installer rather than hardcoding a version.

---

## Privacy promise

### In one paragraph

viewbus does not send telemetry, does not phone home, and has no backend servers. Azure credentials and connection strings are used by the user's machine to talk to Azure directly — they never touch infrastructure operated by viewbus (because there isn't any). The SQLite index, logs, and settings files all live under the user's profile on disk.

### What's on the user's machine

- **SQLite index** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\viewbus\viewbus.db` on Windows; `~/Library/Application Support/viewbus/viewbus.db` on macOS) — resource metadata discovered from Azure or connection strings. Contains no message bodies and no secrets.
- **OS keychain entries** under service name `viewbus` (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain) — raw connection strings the user pastes in. Never written to the index or logs.
- **Settings JSON** (`%APPDATA%\viewbus\settings.json` / `~/Library/Application Support/viewbus/settings.json`) — theme, hotkeys, preferences.
- **Custom themes** in the `themes/` subfolder of the settings directory.
- **Local API discovery file** (`local-api.json`, alongside settings) — the port and a per-launch bearer token for the loopback HTTP API. Regenerated every launch; the listener binds loopback only and rejects requests with an `Origin` header. Disable with `localApi.enabled: false`.
- **Log files** (`…\viewbus\logs\`) — daily-rotated plain-text diagnostics. No PII, no credentials, no message bodies. Attached only if the user opts in via the in-app feedback dialog.

### What leaves the user's machine

Only requests the user triggers:

- Azure authentication (OAuth in the default browser; tokens go directly between Microsoft and the machine).
- Azure Resource Manager + Service Bus REST / AMQP calls (direct to the user's endpoints — the app's CSP allows only `login.microsoftonline.com`, `management.azure.com`, `*.servicebus.windows.net`, and the static viewbus.app hosts below).
- An update check on app start reading `https://viewbus.app/latest.json` — a static JSON file, no query parameters or identifiers. (Microsoft Store installs are also updated through the Store.)
- An announcements check on app start reading `https://viewbus.app/announcements.json` — the same kind of static file; notices that don't apply are filtered locally, dismissed ones remembered in `localStorage`.
- Feedback the user sends from the in-app dialog, plus the log file only if they tick the attach box.

Message bodies an AI assistant reads through the MCP server go to that assistant's provider, which is inherent to asking a model about them. viewbus itself never sees or forwards them.

### The website

`viewbus.app` is a static site on GitHub Pages: no analytics, no cookies, no third-party embeds, fonts self-hosted. GitHub as host sees standard server-log data (IP, user agent, path) under its own privacy statement. The site sets two `localStorage` keys from your own clicks: `viewbus-site-theme` and `viewbus-mcp-client`.

### No third parties

No analytics SDK, no crash reporter, no A/B framework, no affiliate tracking. If a future version adds any of these, it will be opt-in with a clear prompt, and the privacy page will list them.

---

## Support and contact

There is no support email. All routes reach the author directly:

- **Bugs and feature requests:** https://github.com/haakofli/viewbus-site/issues — feature requests are ranked by 👍 reactions and the top ones appear on the home page.
- **Security issues or anything private:** GitHub private vulnerability reporting at https://github.com/haakofli/viewbus-site/security/advisories/new. Also listed in https://viewbus.app/.well-known/security.txt
- **In-app:** Settings → Send feedback, which needs no GitHub account and can optionally attach the local log file.

Data controller for GDPR purposes is Håkon Lia (Norway). viewbus operates no servers, no database, and no account system, so no personal data is held; the supervisory authority is Datatilsynet.

## Terms

viewbus is free of charge but closed source. Users may install it on any number of machines, use it commercially, and build and distribute tools on the local HTTP API and MCP server. Reverse engineering, redistributing modified builds, and selling viewbus are not permitted. The app is provided "as is" with no warranty; liability is limited to the fullest extent permitted by law, and destructive operations (purge, bulk delete, emptying a dead-letter queue) are permanent and the user's responsibility. Governed by Norwegian law. Full text: https://viewbus.app/terms
